extras.price_note: a VPS bills by the month with an hourly rate capped at the monthly figure, so the two columns answer two questions: destroying the box between runs versus keeping it up.
extras.price_basis: 10 h/day column = 300 h at the hourly rate, which is what a server destroyed between runs costs; 24/7 column = the monthly cap, because a VPS kept up all month stops at the cap. From the pinned catalogue card, not re-read.
extras.tiny_price_note: USD 0.000683 an hour at the tiny shape, which is 1 vCPU and 1 GiB. At 10 h/day x 30 that is USD 0.20 a month, against USD 6.89 for the 2 vCPU / 4 GiB column, so the same provider is 34 times cheaper at the smaller shape. The seed's first revision ranked this row at USD 0.03 a month, which was this shape priced as if it were 2 vCPU / 4 GiB; the rank-1 figure was a shape error, and the shape is stock-limited.
extras.shape_scope_note: talaria priced three shapes and this catalogue carries two. The tiny shape is 1 vCPU / 1 GiB, which is the cheapest stock item in either seed pass and the only row here that prices a machine below USD 1 a month. It is not an agent sandbox: 1 GiB cannot hold a browser. Scaleway flags it stock-limited, so it is not guaranteed available.
